rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links Israel's punishment to Moses' earlier promise that God would settle them in the land and test their conduct; he says the period of observation ended after Solomon.
rows.anchor: Mûsâ’nın ilk va‘d ü tebşîrinde وَيَسْتَخْلِفَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرَ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُونَ [el-A‘râf 7/129] buyurulmuş idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's general preference for sinful, unjust rulers amounted in practice to asking God to send people who would bring punishment upon them.
rows.anchor: Bir kavmin böyle bir hâlde bulunması ise yâ Rabbi, bizim başımıza azab ve belâ getirecek kimseler getir gibi bir taleb-i fi‘lîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Nebuchadnezzar, who devastated Israel, killed those able to fight, enslaved women and children, and subjected survivors to taxes and humiliation—the worst worldly punishment.
rows.anchor: ve zürriyetlerini esir, mütebâkīsini de vergilere mahkum eyledi ve onlar bu zillet altında kaldı gitti

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's punishment can arrive immediately when He wills, while His forgiveness and mercy remain without limit for those who repent and follow the Prophet.
rows.anchor: Tevbe edenlere ve sana ittibâ‘eyleyenlere mağfiret ve rahmeti bîpâyândır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the phrase as scattering the Israelites across the earth and dividing them into many communities.
rows.anchor: ve onları, o kavm-i Mûsâ’yı yeryüzünde parça parça ettik, birçok ümmetlere ayırdık.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier organization into twelve tribes under Moses preserved national unity and was a blessing; this later dispersion began their decline and ended their collective power.
rows.anchor: risâlet-i Mûsâ tahtında vahdet-i kavmiyelerini bozmayan bir teşkîlât ve mukaddime-i kemâlleri olan bir nimet idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this dispersion they were scattered throughout the earth and could no longer gather strength.
rows.anchor: Arzın her tarafına perişan bir surette dağıldılar ve artık bir şevket toplayamaz oldular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some of the dispersed Israelites remained righteous, like the believers in Medina who guided by truth and judged by it; others fell below righteousness at varying levels.
rows.anchor: içlerinden bazıları ehl-i salâh Medine’de iman edenler gibi bâlâda geçen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel's state collapsed despite righteous people among them: wicked people were numerous and controlled the community, which represented sin and injustice as a whole.
rows.anchor: dağılmaları içlerinde iyiler hiç bulunmadığından değil, kötülerin kesretinden ve hey’et-i umûmiyesi kötüler elinde bulunup fısk u zulmü temsil etmesinden idi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested the dispersed groups with blessings such as health, wealth, and prosperity and with their opposites; peoples such as the Magi and Romans supplied bitter lessons.
rows.anchor: hem hasenât -sıhhat ve servet ü refah- hem de bunların zıddı seyyiât ile imtihan ettik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trials were meant to turn them from disbelief and sin back to truth and righteousness; some repented, but others did not before Muhammad's era.
rows.anchor: rücû‘edeler küfr ü masiyetten tevbe edip hakka döneler, salâha yüz tutalar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A corrupt later generation inherited the Torah, learned to read and write, and entered teaching, legal-religious, and judicial offices, yet did not uphold its rulings.
rows.anchor: Tevrat seleflerinden bunların ellerine intikal etmiş, okumasını yazmasını öğrenmişler, neşr ü tâlim, iftâ ve hüküm mevki‘lerine geçmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They took fleeting worldly goods and bribes, altered or concealed truth, presumed they would be forgiven, and accepted further bribes without repenting.
rows.anchor: bir rüşvet daha arz olunursa yine alıyorlar, tevbe etmiyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their covenant under the Book required them to say nothing about God except the truth.
rows.anchor: Vaktiyle kendilerinden Allah’a karşı haktan başka bir şey söylemeyeceklerine dair o kitabın mîsâkı alınmadı mı?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They had repeatedly studied the covenant and the truths they now conceal, including the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, and the matters of piety.
rows.anchor: O mîsâkı ve bugün ketm ü tahrif ettikleri hakikatleri, o Resûl, o Nebiyy-i Ümmî, o ittikā meselelerini vaktiyle tekrar tekrar okudular

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı explains the pious as those who avoid injustice, bribery, and illicit gain, and asks whether the offenders will not reason that the afterlife is better for them.
rows.anchor: âhiret evi müttakī olanlar -yani öyle haksızlıktan, rüşvet ü irtikâbdan sakınıp korunanlar- için ayn-ı hayrdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer are reformers whose reward God will not let go to waste.
rows.anchor: ve namazı kılıp kıldıranlar ise

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı frames the following reminder as addressing two covenants: the one imposed on Israel and the universal covenant of primordial human nature.
rows.anchor: biri Benî İsrâil’e yapılmış ilcâ mîsâkı olan, diğeri ale’l-umûm insanlara şâmil fıtrat mîsâkı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads the righteous child as one who grew up and displayed actual righteousness, then had children of his own.
rows.anchor: bir sâlih nesil verdi dilekleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual parents are the later male-female pairs among the original parents' descendants, who occupied their forebears' place as mothers and fathers.
rows.anchor: ilk ananın babanın evlatları veya torunları bulunan ve onların makamına kāim olup ana baba olan erkek ve dişi çiftleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They associated partners with offspring by treating a child as belonging to a nature or harvest deity, a heavenly body such as the sun, or an idol, as in names like servant of the Sun, al-Lat, and al-Uzza.
rows.anchor: Kâh bir tabiatı teşrîk ettiler; meselâ çocuklarını hârisin, bir hars tabiatının, bir hars ma‘bûdunun kulu addettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By this association, human beings who were one community of a single kind were made into different groups; Elmalılı cites Yunus 10:19.
rows.anchor: Esasen cins-i vâhid ümmet-i vâhide olan insanları, bu suretle ecnâs-ı muhtelife hâline getirdiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original human nature contained no shirk; it was introduced later, though its antiquity led people to imagine it an original sin dating from Adam and Eve. God is exalted above it.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı fıtrat-ı ûlâda şirk yoktu, sonradan uyduruldu, bununla beraber o kadar da eskidir ki Âdem ve Havvâ’dan başlamış bir zenb-i aslî zannettiler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı notes the shift from dual forms to the plural يُشْرِكُونَ as a signal concerning the perpetrators of shirk, connected to the rhetorical istihdām he discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: burada cemi‘sîgasıyla يُشْرِكُونَ buyurulması şirkin fâillerinde îzah ettiğimiz istihdâma bir işareti muhtevî olduğundan gaflet edilmemelidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners cannot create anything and are themselves created, so they cannot be partners of the Creator.
rows.anchor: bir şey halk etmez hiçbir şeyin hâlıkı olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols can neither help their worshippers nor defend themselves; a true deity must be invulnerable and able to aid its servants.
rows.anchor: kendi zâtında taarruz olunması mümteni‘ve ibâdına nusret etmeye kādir olmalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols neither follow a call to guidance nor answer prayers, so seeking their help is futile.
rows.anchor: Ne arkanızdan yardım ederler ne de dualarınıza

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı glosses the worshipped beings as enslaved, senseless, unconscious structures like their worshippers, and cautions that the wording's apparent reference to human slaves is not the intended point.
rows.anchor: sizin emsâliniz kullardır. Yani sizin gibi akılsız, şuursuz heyâkil-i memlûkedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended rebuke is that the polytheists themselves resemble the inert idols they worship.
rows.anchor: asıl murad bu değil, kendilerinin, taptıkları esnâm ve evsân gibi

words: قُلِ ٱدْعُوا۟ شُرَكَآءَكُمْ ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنظِرُونِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet challenges the polytheists to summon all their partners and plot against him without delay, showing that he fears no harm from them.
rows.anchor: Haydi bütün şerîklerinizi çağırınız {ثُمَّ كِيدُونِ فَلَا تُنظِرُونِ} sonra hepiniz bana ne hile kurabilirseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, who sends down the Book, is Muhammad's protector, helper, and rescuer, and has revealed that the idolaters are powerless while He supports him.
rows.anchor: her hâlde benim velîm; nâsırım, halâskârım Allah’tır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God becomes the protector and patron of all righteous people.
rows.anchor: Ve bütün sâlihlere O velî ve sâhib olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God cannot rescue their worshippers or themselves.
rows.anchor: ne sizi kurtarabilirler ne de kendilerini kurtarırlar.

words: وَإِن تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ لَا يَسْمَعُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipped beings do not hear calls to guidance and, though they seem to look at people, they do not truly see—whether lacking sight or insight.
rows.anchor: onlar görmezler. Karşılarındaki mevcud ve meşhûda ya bâsıraları

words: وَإِن تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ لَا يَسْمَعُوا۟
rows.speaker: Keşşâf gibi bazı müfessîrin
rows.claim: Some commentators, including the Kashshaf, held that this passage too concerns only idols and said that gems or beads were attached to them to resemble eyes.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf gibi bazı müfessîrin bu beyânâtın da evvelki gibi yalnız esnâma dair olduğuna zâhib olmuşlar

rows.speaker: Keşşâf gibi بعض müfessîrin
rows.claim: To avoid apparent repetition, those commentators distinguished the first passage as a reproach and this one as separating what may from what may not be worshipped.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf gibi bazı müfessîrin bu beyânâtın da evvelki gibi yalnız esnâma dair olduğuna zâhib olmuşlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects the repetition argument: the first passage addresses inanimate idols, while this one concerns the leaders whom the polytheists worship.
rows.anchor: Fakat doğrusu âyette asla tekrar yoktur. Çünkü müşriklerin şürekâsı sade câmid putlardan ibaret değildir.

rows.speaker: Mücâhid, Hasan-ı Basrî ve Süddî
rows.claim: Mujahid, Hasan al-Basri, and Suddi said the pronouns in 'you call them' and 'them' refer to unbelievers; Elmalılı says this is the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid, Hasan-ı Basrî ve Süddî buradaki “ted‘ûhum”, “hum” “hum” zamirleri küffâra ait olduğunu söylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the human leaders, saying they do not hear or see means that the appeal does not enter their ears or eyes.
rows.anchor: Bunlar hakkında “işitmez görmezler” buyurulması da kulaklarına gözlerine girmez demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı adds that no being worshipped besides God can perceive a worshipper's inner anguish, hopes, or desires; a sick person may be watched by loved ones who cannot hear his inward suffering.
rows.anchor: Bir hasta yatar kıvranır, karşısına bütün sevdikleri toplanır, ona bakarlar fakat onun nefsinde neler çektiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All beings worshipped besides God are thus like idols and cannot be directly supplicated for help; God alone hears, sees, and knows the unseen, making worship of others false.
rows.anchor: Allah ise semî‘, basîr, allâmü’l-guyûbdur. Bunun için Allah’tan mâ‘adâsına ta‘abbüd boştur, bâtıldır, hiçtir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Lord of all, God befriends people of faith and good conduct whose natural aptitude remains sound.
rows.anchor: ehl-i salâha, isti‘dâd-ı fıtrîleri bozulmamış olan iman ve hüsn-i hâl sâhiplerine dost olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After proving shirk repugnant to sound innate nature and reason, Elmalılı presents the next verse as the Prophet's instruction in complete righteousness and comprehensive virtue.
rows.anchor: şirk âdetinin örf-i fıtratta ve fıtrat-ı ukūlde nasıl münker olduğu bedâhet derecesinde isbat edildikten sonra salâh-ı ekmeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels close to God, the high assembly, as described in Zumar 39:75.
rows.anchor: buyurulan melâike-i mukarrebîn, mele-i a‘lâ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not disdain worship, glorify God, and prostrate only to Him; the Prophet is told to follow their example.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh sen de öyle yap.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because of this meaning, prostration of recitation is prescribed when this verse is recited.
rows.anchor: bu âyet kıraat edilince secde-i tilâvet meşrû kılınmıştır.

rows.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says that when a person recites and prostrates at a prostration verse, Satan withdraws weeping: the person obeyed and earns Paradise, while Satan disobeyed and faces the Fire.
rows.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm’dan öyle[^1] mervîdir ki Âdemoğlu secde âyetini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through remembrance, worship, and prostration, the way from the Heights to Paradise opens and its rewards are reached.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bu zikr ü ibadet ve secde iledir ki a‘râftan cennete yol açılacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the way to Tabuk, an advance mounted unit of hypocrites mocked the Qur'an and the Prophet, saying he imagined conquering Syria's castles and palaces, which they deemed impossible.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre Resûlullah Tebük’e giderken münafıklardan bir süvari bölüğü de önde gidiyor, aralarında Kur’an ve Peygamber’le istihzâ ediyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God informed the Prophet, who stopped and confronted the group; they denied insulting him or his Companions and claimed they were joking among themselves to shorten the journey.
rows.anchor: yâ nebiyyallah, hayır, vallahi ne senin ne de ashâbının hakkında bir şey değil velâkin birbirimize seferi kısaltmak için dalıp eğleniyorduk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the hypocrites' clasping of their hands as keeping their hands tightly closed, conveying that they withhold their hands.
rows.anchor: münkeri emr, ma‘ruftan nehyederler ve ellerini sıkı tutarlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the mutual awliyāʾ relation as male and female believers being one another's walīs or protectors.
rows.anchor: Erkek, dişi bütün mü’minler ise birbirlerinin velîleridirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good dwellings in Eden are delightful homes in an eternal abode, promised to the spiritual elite, whose beauty human eyes have never seen and hearts never imagined.
rows.anchor: ma‘din-i hayr ve ebedî ikametgâh olan, gözlerin görmediği ve kalb-i beşerin tahattur etmediği cennetlerde gayet dilâviz, saadet ile yaşanacak güzel güzel meskenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pleasure surpasses every other reward because it is the foundation of all good, happiness, honor, and sovereignty; Elmalılı notes it is strikingly not stated directly among the sequence of promises.
rows.anchor: Çünkü her hayr u saadetin, her şeref ü siyâdetin menât ve medârı odur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explanation offered is that God's pleasure is not listed separately because it is realized within every promise and remains continuous in both abodes.
rows.anchor: bunun hikmeti her vaadin zımnında mütehakkık ve dâreynde müstemir olmasındandır denilmiş.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says God asks the people of Paradise if they are content; after their grateful reply, He promises something better—His pleasure and that He will never again be angry with them.
rows.anchor: “Râzı oldunuz mu, hoşnut musunuz?” buyuracak, onlar da
